title: Finding a KARC2 Reflector Without the Birthday Bound
summary: A mirror-slide attack suggests that an appropriate KARC2 reflector could improve security, but finding the choice and proving the improvement remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Determine a choice of reflector for $\mathrm{KARC2}$ under which the birthday-bound term $q^2/2^n$ can be removed from its security bound, and prove the resulting improved security guarantee.

scope.domain: Symmetric cryptography focused on block-cipher design and security bounds for reflection ciphers.
parameters: The reflector choice: the KARC2 construction component whose selection may affect the security bound
q and n: quantities appearing in the birthday-bound term
scope.unresolved_remainder: Find a reflector for KARC2 that removes the birthday-bound term from its security bound and prove the resulting improved security guarantee.

progress.summary: The source presents this as a challenging problem. It says the mirror slide attack suggests that a good reflector may avoid the birthday-bound term, while proving this appears difficult with state-of-the-art techniques.
citation_labels: Tim Beyne et al., Provably Secure Reflection Ciphers
